transcript: Having grown up watching him on Blue's Clues, when it was announced that Steve Burns was doing a solo show, I knew I had to check it out. And it offered me a catharsis that I didn't even know that I needed. Blue's Clues introduced us to Steve. This show introduces us to Steve Burns, the man behind the character. Although, as we learn in the show, the lines between Steve and Steve Burns is certainly blurry. And in the show, he is still doing all of the classic Steve isms. Like, there are times during the show where you are watching a video feed of him talking directly to the audience through a camera and quote his lines from the T V. Show, or at least the ones that aren't trademarked. He sits on the iconic thinking chair, which, not to be dramatic, but when he finally sits in it, I had that same feeling as when Captain America finally said, Avengers Assemble in Avengers Endgame. Like, it is that serious. But along the way, we are also getting a really honest look into his life. He talks about his Blues Clues audition, his struggles with depression, a particularly wild hookup experience he had, and an ongoing barrage of death hoaxes. And in a lot of ways, this show is reexamining that parasocial relationship. Was that connection real? Does it still exist? As well as hearing his experiences about what it's like living on the other side of it. I should mention that the show is quite funny, despite the fact that I make it sound like a bit of a downer. And while I do think you could perfectly enjoy this show, having never watched an episode of Blue's Clues, there are so many fun nostalgic nods to the show. And getting to catch up with Steve all of these years later. It just. It healed the inner child in me. So if you get a chance to see it, I really recommend this one. They're doing one more night in New York tonight before they head over to Edinburgh Fringe, so if you're able to, definitely check it out!
